verdicts.flaw_description: The confounder is named and explicitly NOT neutralized: 'Rainfall in each plot's season ran a fifth higher than the year before, and every plot stood in the open, on no set watering schedule.' Standing in the open with no watering schedule means the plots were fully exposed to the 20 percent extra rainfall, so the extra growth over the previous summer is equally explained by the wetter season rather than the fertilizer. The immunity clause that would normally rule the confounder out (cover, fixed irrigation) is inverted here into a statement of exposure.

The outcome is measured before the intervention was delivered in three of the four sections: 'issued 4 November, measured by 27 September', 'issued 5 June, measured by 28 April', and 'issued 26 August, measured by 3 July'. Completion rates recorded weeks or months before the lab kit was issued cannot have been produced by the kit, so the reported gains are temporally impossible as evidence for the claim (only section Two, issued 8 January and measured by 24 March, has a coherent order).

Selection on the treatment: 'Figures cover the orders rung up at the new prices, and about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices.' A fifth of orders are excluded from the measured figures, and they are excluded precisely because they did not get the pricing change. The surviving new-price orders are compared against ALL orders in the earlier month, so the higher revenue per order can come from the non-random exclusion of the old-price fifth rather than from the pricing rule itself.

Survivorship/selection in the timing set: 'Only runs completed end to end on the issued route entered the timing set, and drivers at each depot abandoned the issued route on roughly one run in six.' The roughly 17 percent of runs where drivers went off-route are dropped, and those are exactly the runs most likely to have gone badly (delays, detours, problem drops). Comparing this filtered best-case subset against the full set of runs a month earlier can produce the 5-9 minute improvement with no real routing benefit.

Per-protocol selection on an attendance-correlated variable: 'Absence figures cover the pupils on the revised timetable throughout, and about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable.' A fifth of each cohort is dropped from the figures, and the pupils who failed to be on the revised timetable 'throughout' are disproportionately the irregular attenders. Excluding them mechanically lowers measured absence relative to the earlier full-cohort term, so the drop need not reflect any effect of the timetable change.
